names.details:
"...In Aſia Minor the religion is the ſame as in Turky in Europe, where only Mahometaniſm is eſtabliſhed, and Chriſtianity of all denominations and Judaiſm are barely tolerated ; ſo that the patriarchs, archbiſhops, and biſhops, whether Greeks or Armenians, as well as their ſees, churches, and congregations, are not only kept under a ſtate of deplorable poverty and ſervitude, but thoſe prelates are depoſed, changed, promoted, or oppreſſed, at the will of the ſultan and his miniſters.

The principal Greek patriarchs, beſides that of Conſtantinople, are thoſe of Jeruſalem, Alexandria, and Antioch. The Armenians have only two of them ; the firſt reſiding at Ecmeſan, a monaſtery in Georgia, and the other at Sis, in Aladulia. Beſides theſe the Neſtorians are allowed one, whose reſidence is commonly at Moſſul, in the province of Diarbeckr.

The archbiſhops belonging to the Greeks are Heraclea, Saloniki, Athens, Malvaſia, Amphipolis, Neapoli di Romania, Lariſſa, Adrianople, Corinth, Nicoſia, Janna, Monembaſia, ...(?), Phanarion, Patras, Proconeſſus, Amaſia, ...(?), Tyre, Tyana, and Berytus..."
